🟦 Computer vision

Pixel

In simple words

One tiny square of a digital picture, stored as numbers that say how bright it is or what colour it has.

One tiny square dot of a digital image. To a computer, a picture is just a grid of pixels, and each pixel is stored as numbers: in a greyscale picture one brightness, usually from 0 (black) to 255 (white); in a colour picture three numbers, for red, green and blue (RGB).

Example. A 12-megapixel phone photo has about 12 million pixels. Zoom in far enough and you'll see the little squares.

Lessons that teach it

  • Lesson 7: How Computers See

Related words

  • Computer visionThe area of AI that helps computers find and recognise things in photos and videos.
  • ConvolutionSliding a small grid of numbers (a filter) across a picture to find patterns such as edges.
  • Convolutional neural network (CNN)A neural network for pictures whose layers use convolutions to find patterns, from edges up to whole objects.
